audit.setting-help: the audit trail: the sink, the forwarding, the rotation, the kill switch

audit-daily.setting-help: also rotate the audit trail at UTC midnight
audit-daily.help: also rotate the audit log at UTC midnight

audit-forward.setting-help: also forward every audit line: the local syslog mirror or a remote collector (the off-box copy)
audit-forward.help: also forward the audit trail: syslog (the local socket auto-scan), syslog:/path (an explicit socket), udp://host[:514] (RFC5426, best-effort) or tcp://host[:514] (RFC6587 framing) — the off-box copy carries the per-writer hash chain, so a scheduled search at the collector can alert on a chain break; docs/AUDIT.md

audit-forward-format.setting-help: the remote forward's envelope: RFC5424 (the default) or CEF — the local syslog forms keep the verbatim send

value-help.cef: the CEF additive wrapping, msg= carries the native line
value-help.rfc5424: the syslog envelope, the native line verbatim in the MSG

audit-forward-format.help: the remote forward's envelope: RFC5424 (the default) or CEF — the local syslog forms keep the verbatim send (remote targets only)

audit-instance.setting-help: the audit lines' instance word: the writer daemon's identity — the control port when unset, the override when spelled
audit-instance.help: the audit lines' instance=<id> word — which daemon wrote the line: the control port when unset/empty (unique per host by construction), the override when spelled; 1-64 characters (letters, digits, . _ : @ -); make an override unique among everything that shares one collector

audit-log.setting-help: the audit trail's file: a path, - for stdout, none = no local file (the forward carries the trail), empty = the XDG state home
audit-log.help: the audit trail: a file path or - for stdout (the docker/journald way); `none` turns the local file off (with a forward spelled that is the remote-only mode); the XDG state home when unset

audit-max-mb.setting-help: rotate the audit trail at this size in MB, keeping N backups; 0 = no size rotation
audit-max-mb.help: rotate the audit log at this size in MB, keeping N backups; 0 = no size rotation

audit/rotate.setting-help: the audit trail's rotation: the size trigger, the UTC-midnight trigger and the backup count

client-timeout.setting-help: disconnect clients silent for this long
client-timeout.help: disconnect clients silent for this many seconds, 0 = never

control.setting-help: the control plane: the tokens, the ops role's RBAC policy, the trusted peers

control-log-replies.setting-help: DEBUG-log the full output of every control command (plainly: the command and its status log)
control-log-replies.help: DEBUG-log the full output of every control command

control-ops-verbs.setting-help: the read-only ops role's RBAC policy: the verbs its sessions may run, comma-separated
control-ops-verbs.help: the read-only ops role's RBAC policy: the verbs its sessions may run, comma-separated

control-port.setting-help: control server target: unix socket path or TCP port on 127.0.0.1
control-port.help: JSON-lines control server target: unix socket path or TCP port number on 127.0.0.1; 0 = off

control-socket-group.setting-help: leave the unix control socket group-accessible (chmod 0660 instead of the plain 0600)
control-socket-group.help: leave the unix control socket group-accessible (chmod 0660 instead of the plain 0600) ($CONTROL_SOCKET_GROUP)

control-token.setting-help: require a token on control connections: the client authenticates with {"cmd": "auth", "token":...}; over the unix socket a trusted peer (root, the daemon's own user or --control-trust-uids — SO_PEERCRED) skips the token (`file:<path>` = the token from an owner-only file)
control-token.help: require a token on control connections: the client authenticates with {"cmd": "auth", "token":...}; over the unix socket a trusted peer (root, the daemon's own user or --control-trust-uids — SO_PEERCRED) skips the token; the value may be `file:<path>` — the first line of an owner-only 0600 file (a systemd LoadCredential rides as file:/run/credentials/...)

control-trust-uids.setting-help: extra peer uids the unix control socket trusts without the token (SO_PEERCRED — a local systemd unit speaks without the secret); root and the daemon's own user are always trusted
control-trust-uids.help: extra peer uids the unix control socket trusts without the token (SO_PEERCRED — a local systemd unit speaks without the secret); root and the daemon's own user are always trusted

control/ops.setting-help: the read-only ops role: the second token that scopes its sessions to the configured verbs (the default: show)

dump.setting-help: the state dump: the live overrides' file, the restore-on-start

dump-interval.setting-help: seconds between the automatic state dumps (the live setting overrides)

value-help.off: only request dump and the shutdown dump

dump-interval.help: seconds between the automatic state dumps, 0 = on request (the request dump command and the shutdown)

dump-key.setting-help: the key that seals the state dumps (the reload's state file too) (`file:<path>` reads an owner-only file)
dump-key.help: the key that seals the state dumps and the reload's state file: the state rides encrypted (an HMAC-SHA256 counter-mode keystream, authenticated — a restore refuses a wrong or missing key, and a configured key refuses an unsealed dump); the reload re-exec re-resolves the same key, so the state file reads on the other side; no key = the dumps stay 0600 plaintext with the integrity hash; a dump path without a key warns at start and on set; the value may be `file:<path>` — the first line of an owner-only 0600 file (a systemd LoadCredential rides as file:/run/credentials/...)

dump-path.setting-help: the state dump file: the live overrides, written on request dump, the graceful shutdown and every dump-interval
dump-path.help: the state dump: the live setting overrides (the tokens apart) as one JSON, written 0600 with an integrity hash (a restore refuses a tampered, unsigned or group-writable dump); dumped on the request dump command, the graceful shutdown and every --dump-interval seconds; loaded on start only with --restore-on-start, on demand with the request restore command

local-time.setting-help: log timestamps in the system time zone instead of UTC
local-time.help: log timestamps in the system time zone instead of UTC

max-clients.help: refuse further connections past this many simultaneous clients, 0 = no limit

max-conn-per-ip.setting-help: simultaneous connections from one peer IP
max-conn-per-ip.help: refuse further connections from one peer IP past this many simultaneous connections, 0 = no per-IP limit

metrics-acl.setting-help: clients allowed to connect to /metrics: "any", "none", comma-separated IPs/prefixes, or file:<path> (the ip-prefix acl file)

value-help.none: no client may connect: every connection is rejected

metrics-acl.help: clients allowed to connect to the /metrics endpoint: "any", "none" (refuse everyone), comma-separated IPs/prefixes like 10.0.0.7,10.48.0.0/16, or "file:<path>" — the standalone ip-prefix acl file (the gate object {"type": "ip-prefix", "rules": [{"type": "allow"|"deny", "prefix": ...}]}: the last matching rule decides, a client no rule decides refuses; "any" = 0.0.0.0/0, the whole space); checked at accept — a client off the ACL is closed without a reply

metrics-client-timeout.setting-help: seconds an idle /metrics client is kept before the socket times out, 0 = the built-in 5 s cap
metrics-client-timeout.help: seconds an idle /metrics client is kept before the socket times out, 0 = the built-in 5 s cap

metrics-max-clients.setting-help: maximum concurrent /metrics clients; extras get an immediate 503, 0 = unlimited
metrics-max-clients.help: maximum concurrent HTTP clients on the /metrics endpoint; extras get an immediate 503, 0 = unlimited

metrics-max-conn-per-ip.setting-help: maximum concurrent /metrics connections from one peer IP, 0 = no per-IP limit
metrics-max-conn-per-ip.help: maximum concurrent /metrics connections from one peer IP, 0 = no per-IP limit

metrics-server.setting-help: the tool's own Prometheus /metrics endpoint (needs a token beyond loopback; the address is --metrics-listen)

value-help.on: serve /metrics on the configured listen address

metrics-server.help: serve the tool's own Prometheus /metrics endpoint (the live `set metrics enable` toggle exists too)

metrics-token.setting-help: the metrics bearer token (Authorization: Bearer) — startup-only (pass it by flag/env/config); the value never renders back (`file:<path>` = the token from an owner-only file)
metrics-token.help: require Authorization: Bearer <token> on the /metrics endpoint (the same scheme the scraper speaks); the value may be `file:<path>` — the first line of an owner-only 0600 file (a systemd LoadCredential rides as file:/run/credentials/...)

modbus-auth.setting-help: the Modbus auth scheme: suite (the crypt handshake) or none

value-help.suite: after every connect, prove the shared key with the suite handshake — the peer answers OK, or ERR and the connection fails

modbus-auth.help: the Modbus auth scheme: `suite` demands the crypt handshake (magic + nonce + HMAC proof of the shared key) right after every connect — the peer answers OK, or ERR and the session drops; none/empty = no auth at all

modbus-interval.setting-help: seconds between polls of the upstream

modbus-profile.setting-help: device profile JSON (a bare name resolves in profiles/profiles/)
modbus-profile.help: device profile JSON (the shared profiles/ schema)

modbus-merge-gap.help: max register gap when merging ranges into block reads, 0 = read ranges separately

modbus-read-delay.setting-help: seconds between consecutive device reads within a poll cycle
modbus-read-delay.help: seconds between consecutive inverter reads within a poll cycle, 0 = no delay

modbus-unit.setting-help: the Modbus unit id the session speaks

restore-on-start.setting-help: the dump loads on start (off: on demand with request restore)
restore-on-start.help: load the state dump when the daemon starts (needs --dump-path) — a restart serves last-known values instead of cold misses; without it the dump loads on demand

config.setting-help: the effective configuration as a set-grammar script (the secret knobs render as *** SECRET REMOVED ***)

knobs.setting-help: the dictionary of all knobs: every knob, its flag, its env twin, its section, how it changes

show.metrics-acl-table: the metrics ACL as its rule chain, one entry per line: allow 0.0.0.0/0 (any), deny 0.0.0.0/0 (none), the whitelist spelled out — or the ip-prefix acl file's own rules with their descs
show.uplink: the inverter link: session counters, per-block latency and errors
show.uplink-sources: the register map: one row per polled register — fc, register, the range that fetches it, source

commands.clear: restore a setting to its configured value: clear <setting>

help.help: describe a word (help <setting>) or map every knob (help config)

request-dump.help: write the state dump: the live setting overrides, sealed (when the daemon has a dump path)

commands.request-reload-config: re-read the config file (the SIGHUP path)

request-restore.help: re-apply a state dump's overrides (when the daemon has a dump path)

commands.show: print a setting's live value, or a report
